subject: Edge route superset learned by incorrect neighbor — staging traffic hairpin
messages:
From: ops@keelco.io
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: pm@keelco.io
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Connectivity flaps after private cutover — intermittent reachability to svc-prod

Hi Dylan,

We started seeing intermittent failures to svc-prod (10.40.18.0/24) after the cutover at ~08:40 PT. A subset of requests are routing to our staging stack (10.40.0.0/16) and then getting dropped on return — looks like a hairpin that times out after 6s.

Attached is a tcpdump and a traceroute from our egress (keelco-trace.txt).

Symptoms:
- Clients to svc-prod succeed ~80% but then intermittently fail with TCP retransmits.
- When a failure happens, traceroute shows traffic entering Redwood edge, then routed to 10.40.0.0/16 (staging) instead of exact /24.
- We think a superset route (/16 or /22) is being learned somewhere and taking precedence.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing a /16 from our side or if the edge is misadvertising?

Thanks,
Nate
KeelCo NetOps

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Connectivity flaps after private cutover — need edge routing review

Attaching KeelCo trace and our initial packet captures. Short summary: KeelCo reports 10.40.18.0/24 should be the only advertised prefix for prod; staging sits inside 10.40.0.0/16. After cutover, some traffic to 10.40.18.0/24 is arriving at our edge and being forwarded into the 10.40.0.0/16 staging VLAN (hairpin) — we see asymmetric return failures.

Key artifacts (routes-snapshot.csv attached):
- Redwood edge RIB (edge-01) at 09:00 PT: shows a learned route 10.40.0.0/16 via bgp neighbor 203.0.113.7 (KeelCo-agg) with localpref 100. More specifics (/24) present as OSPF/connected in some moments.
- Conntrack/stateful logs show dropped replies where the source IP matches 10.40.18.x but return path uses staging path and hits an SG that only allows 10.40.18.0/24 as source — result: return packets dropped.

Hypothesis: KeelCo accidentally advertised a superset aggregate (either /16 or /22) from one of their routers during the cutover; our edge accepted the superset and pulled traffic into staging VLAN where SG rules block the return because the stateful sessions were pinned to prod path.

Requesting:
1) Karthik/Mina please confirm RIB history and origin of /16 on edge-01 (timestamps in routes-snapshot.csv).
2) Vanessa, can you check SG logs for the staging subnet for rejects around 08:40–09:20?
3) If superset is confirmed, propose immediate remediation: prefer more-specific static (/24) on edge or ask KeelCo to withdraw aggregate and re-advertise more specifics.

Thanks — D

---

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Connectivity flaps after private cutover — need edge routing review

Short findings from edge-01 RIB and bgp updates (09:00–09:20 PT window):
- At 08:42 PT, edge-01 received a BGP UPDATE from 203.0.113.7 with NLRI 10.40.0.0/16, AS_PATH origin showing internal KeelCo aggregator (they accidentally turned on a summary policy).
- More-specific 10.40.18.0/24 was present earlier, but the /16 replaced the /24 in our RIB while agg was active. When the /16 withdrew (09:17 PT), the /24 reappeared and connectivity normalized.

Impact analysis:
- Hairpin: Because the /16 pointed to a different next-hop that maps into our staging VLAN, traffic for prod was forwarded into staging, which then blocked stateful returns (SGs in staging permit only specific prod source ranges; reverse path did not match TCP state).
- MTU/Fragmentation: Not observed here; packet sizes were small and retransmits were caused by TCP state loss rather than fragmentation.

Immediate remediation options (ranked):
1) (Fast) Install a locally-preferred static /24 on edge-01 for 10.40.18.0/24 with higher localpref to prefer the correct KeelCo eBGP neighbor until KeelCo withdraws the aggregate.
2) (Recommended) Ask KeelCo to withdraw the /16 aggregate and re-advertise the /24s. They should avoid summary during active cutovers.
3) (Mitigation) Temporarily relax SG source checks in staging to allow return path while we fix routing — low-confidence due to security risk.

I can push the static if you approve; it’s a quick change (non-disruptive to other prefixes). I also recommend a post-mortem with KeelCo to add a cutover playbook item: explicitly avoid aggregates and verify longest-prefix matching at both edges.

-Karthik
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Nate, thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. Karthik confirmed an accidental /16 aggregate was accepted by our edge and temporarily supplanted the /24. That explains the hairpin and the stateful return failures.

Proposed immediate action:
- Redwood to install a preferred static for 10.40.18.0/24 on edge-01 (non-disruptive). Karthik is ready to apply with a 10s maintenance window.
- KeelCo to withdraw the aggregate (/16) and re-announce the /24s. Please confirm withdrawal ETA.
- I’ve attached the relevant playbook excerpt (redwood-playbook-private-cutover.pdf) and our suggested validation checklist.

If you’re comfortable, we’ll apply the static at 12:30 PT and ask KeelCo to withdraw by 12:40 PT so we don’t get a race. Please confirm.

—Dylan

From: ops@keelco.io

Cc: pm@keelco.io, nate@keelco.io
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Connectivity flaps after private cutover — route aggregate withdrawn, monitoring

Confirmed — we inadvertently had a summary policy toggle on one of our aggregation routers. We withdrew 10.40.0.0/16 at 12:36 PT and re-advertised the /24s. Post-withdrawal traces attached (keelco-trace.txt).

Outcome:
- We observed restored stable connectivity to svc-prod within 30–60s of the withdraw.
- No further hairpin traces in the monitoring window.

Action items agreed:
- KeelCo will remove the summary-policy from their cutover playbook and add explicit pre/post checks (JIRA-NR-9834).
- Redwood to keep the static /24 in place for 24h as a safety guard; Karthik to remove after no recurrence.

Thanks for the fast turnaround.

—Nate (KeelCo NetOps)

[Attachments: keelco-trace.txt, redwood-playbook-private-cutover.pdf]
